|  Module Number:   | **14901**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **EUNICE Individual Pathway Master's Module**  |  
|  EUNICE Individuelles Master-Modul   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 5 - Business, Law and Social Sciences   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. Dr. rer. pol. habil. Berger, Wolfram 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | Students can flexibly choose and aggregate educational offerings / learning opportunities from partner universities within the EUNICE university alliance. In doing so, they acquire both subject-specific and interdisciplinary competencies in an international learning environment and strengthen their capacity to independently select, combine, and integrate learning outcomes into their individual study pathways. Through in-person, digital or hybrid teaching and collaboration with students and lecturers from other countries, they develop intercultural competencies and actively contribute to the formation of a European identity. Overall, the module fosters openness, self-organisation, and the ability to purposefully make use of diverse and complementary educational offerings**.**  |  
| Contents:  |  The module functions as an umbrella module for a wide range of learning opportunities within the European University Alliance EUNICE. Students select and aggregate learning opportunities from partner universities within the EUNICE university alliance up to a total of 6 ECTS. Depending on the selected offerings, the format of instruction may vary. It enables the individual selection and purposeful utilisation of learning opportunities offered by EUNICE partner universities, such as joint courses, MOOCs, Blended Intensive Programmes, or language courses. These learning opportunities are selected independently by students in line with their academic interests and study progress and are integrated into the module following consultation with the module coordinator. Intercultural exchange and collaboration with students from partner universities are regarded as integral and valuable components of the module.   |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | Depending on the selected EUNICE offerings.  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Self organised studies / 180 Hours

| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | Made available in the respective courses.  |

| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | The examination requirements for the selected courses can be found in the [ _EUNICE course catalog_](https://eunice-university.eu/) in the corresponding study guides and form the basis for grading and certificate issuance.  |
